answer: The falcon mechanism resists Sybil attacks by having AI agents stake reputation at each nadir of their operational pulse. When an agent attempts to create multiple fake identities, it must duplicate this staked reputation across each sybil node. The nadir represents the minimum reputation threshold required for participation, while the pulse measures the agent's activity frequency. By forcing attackers to duplicate stakes at each nadir, the mechanism makes mass fake identity creation economically prohibitive, as each sybil requires the same reputation investment as a single authentic agent.
